title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page opens by closing a notational digression from the previous page. Grothendieck keeps the provisional notation (M_{ρ,σ}, M~_{ρ,σ}, the various primes, ~, ♮) for now and promises a later special § to revise it. He had noted that the symbol ~ is overloaded: it appears both in Γ_Q~ and M~_{0,3} and in the quotient M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ ≃ M~_{ρ,σ}.

Setting. This is the 'Longue Marche' continuation on the profinite Teichmüller tower in genus 1. The universal group is M = N~_{1,1}, an extension of Γ_Q~ by SL(2,Z)^. Here:
- ρ and σ are the torsion elements, presumably of orders 4 and 6, attached to the orbifold points j = 1728 and j = 0 of M_{1,1}.
- ω is presumably the central element −1.
- λ_0 and λ_1 are presumably standard loops/generators coming from π_1 of P^1 minus 3 points.
- N_ρ and Z_ρ are a normalizer and a centralizer.
- G_{ρ,σ} and G^G_{ρ,σ} are auxiliary subgroups.
- Φ_{12} is apparently an abelian 'multiplier' group (Φ^2_{12}, Φ^*_{12}) whose elements μ carry integer invariants ν = ν(μ), ν'', ν_3, written μ = (ν_2, ν_3, ν_0) on the next page. It plausibly relates to Z/12 = SL(2,Z)^ab.

The groups M~_{ρ,σ}(−J̄) and M'~_{ρ,σ}(−J̄) are presumably subgroups cut out by a condition at, or attached to, the point labelled J (the j-invariant).

Content of (211). M~_{ρ,σ} is written as a semidirect product Φ^*_{12} ⋉ (G_a × G^+); the letter G_a vs G_m is unclear, and the next page writes G_m. Elements are written (λ, x).μ. The subgroup M~_{ρ,σ}(−J̄) is the set of those elements with x·u_μ ∈ N_ρ. Here x·u_μ lies in G_{ρ,σ}, and u_μ is the element defined earlier in (151), with u_μ(ρ) = λ_1^ν ρ.

Content of (212). By the earlier formula (154), v = σ^{ν_3} δ^{−ν''} u_μ, with δ = λ_1 λ_0^{−1}, lies in ΓN_ρ and has invariant X(v) = μ. Writing σ = ω τ' τ, one gets v = τ'^{ν_3}(ω^{ν_3} · τ^{ν_3} δ^{−ν''} u_μ). Each of the three factors lies in ΓG^G_{ρ,σ}, so v ∈ ΓN_ρ ∩ G^G_{ρ,σ} = ΓZ^G_ρ.

The next page uses this to describe the fibre of N_ρ over μ as {ω^i σ^{−ν_3} δ^{−ν''} u_μ}, and hence M~_{ρ,σ}(−j) and M'~_{ρ,σ}(−j) explicitly as in (213) and (214).

Overall, the page is a step in computing normalizer/centralizer-type subgroups of the extended Galois–Teichmüller group of M_{1,1} attached to the elliptic points. It is technical bookkeeping inside a long computation.
errors: Ambiguity between G_a here and G_m on the next page for the λ-component. The semidirect-product factor is presumably multiplicative (G_m); G_a looks like a slip or mis-writing.
Sign inconsistency in the exponent of σ: here (154) gives v = σ^{ν_3} δ^{−ν''} u_μ, while the next page writes ω^i σ^{−ν_3} δ^{−ν''} u_μ.
Equation number (212) is used both on this page and on the next page for different formulas.
The defining condition of M~_{ρ,σ}(−J̄) is written with a question mark ('∈ N_ρ ?'), so Grothendieck himself flags it as tentative.
The claim that each of the three factors τ'^{ν_3}, ω^{ν_3}, τ^{ν_3}δ^{−ν''}u_μ lies in ΓG^G_{ρ,σ} is asserted without verification on this page; it depends on earlier definitions not visible here.

ideas.what: Writing a 'multiplier' subgroup M~_{ρ,σ} of the extended Galois–Teichmüller group in genus 1 as a semidirect product Φ*_{12} ⋉ (G_m × G^+), and cutting out subgroups by normalizer conditions at the elliptic points ρ (order 4) and σ (order 6)
ideas.modern_name: Galois action / decomposition-type groups at the orbifold points j=0, 1728 of M_{1,1}; normalizers of torsion in SL(2,Z)^ ⋊ Γ_Q-type extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (1990s, genus-1 Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme (M_{1,1}, SL(2,Z)^, the Teichmüller tower) is in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche; these explicit computations are not.

ideas.what: Explicit element v = σ^{ν_3} δ^{−ν''} u_μ (δ = λ_1 λ_0^{−1}) realizing a given multiplier μ inside the normalizer N_ρ, and lying in the centralizer Z^G_ρ
ideas.modern_name: Explicit lifts / sections of the multiplier (cyclotomic-character-type) map on normalizers of torsion elements

ideas.what: Notational plan: replace ~ in Γ_Q~ by a superscript such as 'ét' (étendu) or 'gén' (généralisé), to be revised in a later dedicated §

missed.claim: Grothendieck plans a systematic description of the subgroups M~_{ρ,σ}(−J̄) and M'~_{ρ,σ}(−J̄) of the genus-1 extended Galois–Teichmüller-type group attached to the elliptic points. The explicit formulas (213)–(214) on the next page give such a description. It is unclear whether this explicit semidirect-product description has been matched in the literature on GT acting on M_{1,1}.
missed.quote: Il faudrait aussi décrire les sous-groupes M~_{ρ,σ}(−J̄), M'~_{ρ,σ}(−J̄) dans M~_{ρ,σ} écrit comme un produit semi-direct
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a possibly independent, explicit treatment of 'decomposition groups' at j=0, 1728 in the profinite/Galois setting of M_{1,1}. It could be compared with Nakamura's and Lochak–Schneps' work, but it appears to be routine bookkeeping.

deep.surprise_reason: Technical intermediate bookkeeping (normalizer/centralizer computations and a notational aside) inside a long genus-1 Teichmüller-tower computation. It is interesting as documentation of how far Grothendieck pushed explicit computations, but nothing here stands out as a self-contained new result.
transcription_corrections: Top page number reads '694' (Grothendieck's own numbering within pages 650 bis–787), not '894'.
In (211) the semidirect product appears as Φ*_{12}(G_a × G^+), with a script/underlined G or 𝔊 and superscript +. Below it, the elements are labelled λ ∈ G_a, x ∈ G^+, μ ∈ Φ^2_{12}.
u_μ(ρ) = λ_1^{ν} ρ (conjugation-type formula, not λ_1^ν(ρ)). The struck-out continuation reads λ_1^{3ν''} λ_1^{−ν_3} ρ.
The struck-out line reads (x u_μ)(ρ) = x(λ_1)^ν x(ρ), followed by 'on aura (154)'.
In (212) the first factor is τ'^{ν_3}; the final line reads '∈ ΓN_ρ ∩ G^G_{ρ,σ} = ΓZ^G_ρ' (the transcription has this correctly).
